Needs changes before merge. One P3 finding remains.

**Requested before merge**

1. `crates/motion/src/machining3d/reentry.rs:26`: prove the full tool disc clear before you keep a straight restart.

   `plunge_law::into_solid` checks the central core of a non-centre-cutting tool. It does not prove the full disc clear, as #3670 requires. With radius 3 mm, an earlier cut within 1.5 mm of the axis makes this check return false.

   The catalog still posts this restart at `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.nc:1402`:

   ```gcode
   G00 X-0.139 Y-20.062 Z47.
   G01 X-0.139 Y-20.062 Z10. F300.
   ```

   I checked the saved moves and the actual OBJ mesh independently:

   - The exact restart axis is `(-0.138840, -20.062037)`.
   - The stock point `(-0.138840, -17.800000, 10)` is 2.262037 mm from that axis, inside the cutter.
   - Every earlier cut that reaches Z10 stays at least 3.68 mm from that point, outside the 3 mm cutting radius. The nearest cut is the row at Y-21.48. This check also includes a conservative bound over each earlier helix.
   - The OBJ surface at that point is Z8.582312. Thus the point at Z10 contains uncut stock. The previous level reaches only Z12.

   The central core is clear, but the outer part of the cutter still plunges into stock. The new catalog test passes because `first_solid_plunge` uses the same core test.

   Keep the core law for non-centre-cutting tools. Use a full-disc clearance proof for this restart policy. Add a test that checks the outer stock independently of the core predicate. Then regenerate the two catalog files.

**What looks good**

- Candidate entries run on copies. Rejected candidates do not remain in the path.
- The new module has a provenance note. The change adds no dependency, command, UI change, or process change.

Addressed: prove the full cutter disc clear before a straight restart. The restart axis must lie on an earlier straight cut at or below its depth. The core law stays unchanged.

Pins: `machining3d::reentry::tests::cleared_core_does_not_prove_the_outer_disc_clear` and `catalog_3d_rough_finish::pocket_re_entry_keeps_the_outer_stock_clear`. Head: `ea39d4180e62646a463a9b4fa91e3f5464d95254`.

Checks: quick passed all 57 steps. Clippy passed with no warnings. Light passed six steps and 11 tests. Heavy: RED: 103 steps, one unexpected failed step, zero stalls. The bore test expects `(3158, 3130, 1141)` but gets `(4688, 4660, 1980)`. The original reviewed source gives the same counts and failure. All preceding safety checks pass. This pre-existing count pin stays unchanged. Five other test failures are normalized as expected: three for #1950, one for #3825, and one for #2849.

Please review this head again.

Ready for the maintainer to merge. No blocking findings remain.

**Previous finding**

1. Full-disc clearance: fixed by `ea39d4180e62646a463a9b4fa91e3f5464d95254`.
   `disc_into_solid` requires an earlier straight cut on the restart axis, at or below the restart depth. It excludes arcs.
   The separate core law stays unchanged. The new unit tests and the independent OBJ catalog test pass.
   Both catalog files were regenerated. The earlier restart at `(-0.138840, -20.062037, 10)` now uses an entry move.

I checked the author's Addressed comment and each part of the earlier finding. No new blocker was found.
The clean review replaces `needs-rework` with `merge-ready`.

**What looks good**

- The full-disc proof is conservative. An offset centre line cannot grant clearance.
- Candidate entries run on copies. Rejected candidates do not remain in the path.
- The independent catalog test reads the OBJ surface and earlier cutting sweeps. It calls neither production clearance predicate.
- The new module has a provenance note and a decision record. The PR adds no dependency, UI change, command, or process change.

**Goldens moved**

Both changed catalog files appear under Goldens moved in the PR body:

- `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.nc`
- `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.camproj`

The saved pocket path has 2,462 moves, up from 2,021 on upstream main. Straight plunges decrease from 71 to zero.
The replacements are helical entries or ramps along the passes. The two posted finish sections are byte-identical.
Both finish cached move arrays are unchanged. The catalog suites pass their regeneration and posting checks.

**Pre-existing heavy failure, non-blocking**

I checked the heavy failure reported in the body with this exact command:

```text
cargo test --release -j6 -p camcraft-app --test pocket3d_hsm the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean -- --ignored --exact
```

It fails on the trial merge and on bare upstream main `9046e1dc80d266f7dcc1ed04acd052e874bac81a`.
Both runs reach the same final count assertion at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:157`:

```text
expected: (3158, 3130, 1141)
actual:   (4688, 4660, 1980)
```

The preceding safety assertions pass. The counts and planner notes are identical in both runs.
This failure is not caused by this PR. Related tracking: [#2371](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/2371) for macOS bore counts, and [#1852](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/1852) for heavy count drift.
I did not run the full heavy lanes. Current upstream law does not require them for this P3 PR.
